security_audit.summary: The 154 static matches are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, normal shell capture, documentation links, cache paths, secret references, and identifier names. remediation.issue: Unquoted GitHub Actions values are inserted into run commands.
remediation.suggestion: Pass expressions through environment variables, quote every expansion, and validate topology, filename, and package values against strict allowlists.

remediation.issue: Examples execute packages selected by mutable tags or no version.
remediation.suggestion: Pin npm packages to reviewed exact versions and GitHub Actions to immutable commit SHAs. Remove the global alpha-tag installation.

semantic_findings.title: Unquoted GitHub Actions Values Enter Shell Commands
semantic_findings.description: Workflow examples interpolate reusable-workflow inputs, changed filenames, and generated package names directly into shell command text. Crafted values can add shell syntax and execute unintended commands.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited run blocks place expression results in shell command positions without quoting or validation. GitHub substitutes these values before the shell parses the command.

semantic_findings.title: Mutable Third-Party Packages Execute Without Immutable Pins
semantic_findings.description: Examples run ruv-swarm through npx without a version and install claude-flow from the mutable alpha tag. A compromised or changed package can execute during workflow generation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The commands explicitly execute packages selected by an omitted version or a mutable distribution tag. npm package execution occurs with the current user or runner permissions.

content.user_title: Automate GitHub Workflows with AI Coordination
content.value_statement: Complex GitHub Actions pipelines are difficult to coordinate, optimize, and maintain. This skill provides workflow templates, swarm commands, security patterns, monitoring guidance, and repository automation examples.
actual_capabilities: Provides commands for generating and optimizing GitHub Actions workflows.
Documents coordination modes for pull requests, issues, releases, repositories, reviews, CI, and security.
Supplies workflow examples for testing, scanning, deployment, releases, caching, and monorepos.
Shows failure analysis, cost optimization, resource analysis, and workflow profiling commands.
Demonstrates Claude-Flow MCP coordination and concurrent GitHub CLI operations.
limitations: Requires GitHub CLI authentication plus external ruv-swarm and Claude-Flow packages.
Examples require review and adaptation for repository permissions, branch rules, and deployment environments.
The skill provides documentation only and includes no bundled validation or test suite.
Mutable package references and unquoted workflow values require security corrections before production use.

use_cases.title: Build a Repository CI Pipeline
use_cases.description: Create a language-aware workflow plan with parallel tests, caching, security checks, and clear permissions.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Pull Request Maintenance
use_cases.description: Plan automated validation, review comments, issue updates, and failure diagnosis across active pull requests.

use_cases.title: Harden Workflow Automation
use_cases.description: Review workflow permissions, secret handling, dependency pins, deployment gates, and shell interpolation risks.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic CI Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this repository and propose a basic GitHub Actions CI workflow. Identify languages, test commands, required permissions, and caching. Do not modify files until I approve.
prompt_templates.scenario: Starting GitHub Actions for a repository

prompt_templates.title: Optimize an Existing Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review .github/workflows/[file] for slow or duplicated work. Recommend parallel jobs, dependency caching, timeouts, and least-privilege permissions. Show expected tradeoffs before editing.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose a Failed Run
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect GitHub Actions run [run-id] with gh. Summarize failed jobs, likely root causes, and safe fixes. Retry only after confirming no destructive side effects.

prompt_templates.title: Design Secure Monorepo Automation
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a reusable monorepo workflow for [packages]. Generate a validated dynamic matrix, parallel tests, security checks, and staged deployment. Pin dependencies and prevent expression injection. Require approval before publishing.

output_examples.input: Optimize our Node.js pull request workflow for speed.
output: Finding: dependency installation repeats across three jobs.
Recommendation: use one keyed npm cache and separate lint, test, and security jobs.
Expected result: shorter feedback time with unchanged required checks.
Failure: the integration job cannot reach its test database.
Likely cause: the service health check finishes after the test command starts.
Next step: add a bounded readiness check, then rerun only the failed job.
Detect changed packages and validate every generated matrix value.
Run package tests in parallel with read-only default permissions.
Require environment approval before publishing signed artifacts.

best_practices: Review generated workflows and diffs before running repository mutations.
Pin actions and packages, declare minimal permissions, and protect deployment environments.
Quote shell variables and validate every value derived from events, inputs, files, or tool output.
anti_patterns: Do not run mutable packages or actions with repository secrets.
Do not interpolate GitHub expressions directly into shell command text.
Do not enable automatic deployment, release, or merge operations without approval gates.

faq.question: Does this skill change repositories automatically?
faq.answer: It can guide commands that create workflows, issues, pull requests, releases, and deployments. Require review before running mutating commands.

faq.question: What tools are required?
faq.answer: Most examples require Node.js, GitHub CLI authentication, ruv-swarm, and sometimes Claude-Flow.

faq.question: Can it optimize existing workflows?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents analysis commands for parallelization, caching, cost, resources, failures, and performance.

faq.question: How should credentials be handled?
faq.answer: Use GitHub secrets or OIDC, grant minimal permissions, and expose credentials only to pinned, reviewed steps.

faq.question: Does it support monorepos?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples cover changed-package detection, dynamic matrices, parallel builds, and coordinated releases.

faq.question: Are the examples production ready?
faq.answer: No. Validate inputs, quote shell values, pin dependencies, review permissions, and test workflows in a restricted environment first.
